data: © Soviet Academy of Sciences / Intercosmos (historical). Lander + the first atmospheric balloon probe; surface experiments triggered early. Position: NASA NSSDCA catalogue.

Two days before reaching Venus, Vega 1 split in two: a capsule carrying a lander and a balloon entered the atmosphere on 11 June 1985, while the main spacecraft flew on towards Halley's Comet. The balloon floated in the clouds about 54 km up for some 46 hours — the first instrument balloon flown on another planet. Turbulence during the descent set off the lander's surface experiments, the soil drill among them, about 20 km up, so it never sampled the ground. On 6 March 1986 the spacecraft passed Halley's nucleus at about 8,900 km.
